keyVerseText: And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew verb שָׂטַם (sâṭam) is a primitive root that fundamentally conveys the idea of harboring animosity or opposition. Its core sense involves a deliberate, inward posture of hatred or grudge-bearing, often with an element of lurking or persecuting intent. This literal sense adds depth to the English gloss 'hate' by emphasizing not only emotional dislike but also a sustained, active opposition against another person.
usageInScripture: This verb appears six times in Scripture, consistently conveying the notion of hatred or opposition toward a person. Translations such as 'hated,' 'at him and hated him,' and 'they hate' reveal a range that includes both personal animosity and collective opposition. The consistency of this word's usage highlights a persistent, heartfelt antagonism rather than a fleeting or superficial dislike.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding שָׂטַם in its original sense enriches our grasp of human brokenness and the reality of enmity that sin engenders between individuals. This word captures the deep-seated opposition that can arise even within families, as seen in biblical narratives. From a Christian perspective, recognizing this animosity underscores the need for divine reconciliation through Christ, who overcomes hatred by embodying perfect love and forgiveness. It also calls believers to examine their own hearts for any lingering grudges that hinder peace and unity.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 27:41 states, 'And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.' Here, שָׂטַם vividly conveys Esau's deep-seated hatred and hostile intent toward Jacob. The word emphasizes not only Esau's emotional resentment but also his readiness to act violently, revealing the destructive power of cherished animosity within a family.
